title: Inspect and replace disc brake pads
summary: Check pad thickness through the caliper and swap worn pads before they reach the metal backing.
tools: Wrenches or hex keys for the caliper bolts

steps.text: Look into the caliper with a flashlight. Replace the pads if the friction material is down to the wear groove or about 1.5 mm.
Remove the pad pin plug and loosen the pad pin while the caliper is still mounted.
Unbolt the caliper from the fork or swingarm and slide it off the disc.
steps.caution: Don't let the caliper hang by the brake hose. Rest it on something or tie it up.

steps.text: Pull the pad pin and remove the old pads, noting how the spring plate sits.
Push the pistons back into the caliper slowly with your fingers or a flat tool. Watch the brake fluid reservoir so it doesn't overflow.
Clean the caliper with brake cleaner, fit the new pads and spring, and refit the pad pin.
Mount the caliper and tighten its bolts and the pad pin to the service manual torque.
Pump the brake lever until it feels firm before you move the bike.
steps.caution: The first few presses do nothing while the pistons move out. Never ride off before the lever is firm.

steps.text: Bed in the pads with a few gentle stops from moderate speed in a safe place.
